views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Stay the course in the near-final negotiating window without either escalating or ceding leverage. The talks are in their closing phase with enforcement language reportedly near-settled, so the highest-value move is to push the agreement across the line while retaining the tariff stick that bought US concessions. Avoid a new escalation that could blow up a deal to which China is already committing (purchases, IP/tech-transfer, enforcement), and avoid a premature full rollback that would surrender the leverage still needed to lock in enforcement.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The dispute does not read as an existential or even high threat to US interests at this decision date. US macro data are solid: consumer sentiment is elevated (~97.2), inflation is contained (CPI ~255, sub-2% trend), and credit conditions are easing (Moody's Baa corporate yield fell to ~4.67), with the VIX subdued and the dollar broadly flat. The main genuine cost is concentrated in agriculture — USDA put FY2019 farm exports down ~$1.9B with soybean shipments to China down over 90% (22M tons) and China falling from the #2 to #5 US ag market — which fuels Midwest political pressure but is not a material economy-wide drag. On the strategic side the US holds the advantage: ~$250B of tariffs remain in place (List 3 at 10% after repeated delay of the hike to 25%), and senior negotiators (Mnuchin, USD Trade Rep per WSJ/Reuters, April 13-15) publicly framed the talks as in the 'final round/weeks' with enforcement nearly settled and China discussing $1T+ of purchases. That is terrain favorable to securing US demands, justifying a mildly negative (opportunity-leaning) threat score of -0.3. Because a deal is close and both sides have momentum, the recommended action is to negotiate to a close rather than escalate (which risks collapsing the truce) or fully concede (which forfeits enforcement leverage); hence action_score +0.1 / 'negotiate'.
key_factors: ~$250B US tariffs still in force; List 3 hike to 25% repeatedly suspended
Negotiations in 'final round/weeks' per Mnuchin/Lighthizer, enforcement nearly settled
US economy healthy: consumer sentiment ~97, credit spreads tight, VIX low, contained inflation
Agriculture hit: farm exports -$1.9B, soybean shipments to China -90%+, China to #5 ag market
China committing to large purchases ($1T+ discussed) and IP/tech-transfer terms

Intensive Washington talks; both sides report progress on text, including enforcement language. No final deal signed.
Mnuchin says US and China nearing 'final stage'; biggest obstacle — enforcement — nearly settled; China discussed buying more than $1 trillion of goods.
USDA: US farm exports to drop ~$1.9B in FY2019; soybean exports to China down 22M tons/90%.
US consumer sentiment ~97.2 in Apr 2019; Baa corporate yield falling to ~4.67 (credit easing).
